description: Automerge is gated on CI: every rule below merges only after the audit job (frozen install, syntax check, sanitizer unit tests, full OAuth + MCP smoke test, pnpm audit) and the multi-arch image build go green on the PR. Anything CI cannot judge — a major, a change to the tool surface the LLM sees — stays manual.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Renovate's default for security PRs is minimumReleaseAge: null — no cooldown at all. pnpm has no such exemption: pnpm-workspace.yaml sets minimumReleaseAge: 1440, and it is enforced both when Renovate resolves the lockfile and when CI verifies it, so a zero-cooldown security PR lands as a package.json bump with no matching lockfile and CI that cannot pass. Wait out pnpm's window — and no longer — so security fixes still jump the 3-day queue with a lockfile that installs. They are not automerged: a CVE fix is exactly the change worth reading, and it publishes an image the moment it lands.

packageRules.description: Every npm dep change ships in the image, so bump the wrapper version in the same PR — a new image tag gets published and downstream pins (Renovate) pick it up. Patch and minor automerge; the smoke test boots the real server and drives the whole OAuth flow, so a dep that breaks it cannot reach main.
Upstream Lunch Money tools: minor bump (the tool surface Claude sees changed) and reviewed manually — tool changes alter what an LLM can do to the finances
Distroless runtime is a rolling tag pinned by digest; digest bumps are routine security patches. No version bump — the weekly rebuild refreshes bases under the existing tag either way
Builder image. A Node minor or patch is exercised by the same PR build that produces the image, so nothing else is gating it.

GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests, and a stale pin is its own supply-chain risk. Grouped so a round of digest bumps is one PR instead of eight, and automerged — the workflow that would break is the one running on the PR.

The compose example pins the image this repo publishes, so this update only ever trails a release that already passed CI. It touches no file the version-bump guard watches, so automerging it just keeps the docs honest without a second release.

No major ever automerges — not express, not the MCP SDK, not pnpm, not the Node or distroless base. Placed after the automerge rules so it overrides all of them; the npm rule's bumpVersion still applies, so a major arrives as a reviewable PR that already carries its version bump.
